review_candidates.title: Head of Americas Talent Acquisition
review_candidates.description: Job Description About Agilent Agilent Technologies is a global leader in life sciences, diagnostics, and applied chemical markets, delivering instruments, software, services, and consumables that advance the quality of life. Our solutions help scientists and clinicians answer some of the world's most important questions — from developing new therapeutics and advancing cancer diagnostics to ensuring the safety of food, water, and the environment. Headquartered in Santa Clara, California, Agilent employs approximately 18,000 people worldwide serving laboratories across pharma, biotech, clinical, chemical, environmental, food, academic, and government markets. The Role Agilent Global TA is conducting a search for a Head of Americas Talent Acquisition to lead hiring strategy and execution across the Americas. As a member of the Talent Acquisition Leadership Team (TALT) this leader will own the full recruiting engine for the Americas region — leading a team of Lead TA Partners, Senior TA Partners, and TA Partners - collaborating with senior business and functional leaders on workforce planning, and building the processes, tools, and employer brand that allow Agilent to attract exceptional scientific, engineering, commercial, and operations talent. The talent we hire directly shapes our ability to innovate for the lab of the future — this is a high-visibility leadership role at the heart of that mission. What You'll Do Leadership & Strategy Own the Americas talent acquisition strategy, translating business goals and headcount plans into an executable hiring roadmap across R&D, manufacturing, field service, commercial, and corporate functions Lead, coach, and develop a team of Lead/Senior/TA Partners; set clear goals, develop talent, and build a high-performance, inclusive team culture aligned with the One Agilent values of integrity, respect, teamwork, and accountability Serve as a trusted advisor to executives and hiring leaders on org design, market intelligence, compensation trends, and the availability of specialized talent — from analytical chemists and molecular biologists to software engineers and field service professionals Partner with Finance and HR leadership on annual and quarterly workforce planning, capacity modeling, and hiring prioritization Execution & Operations Drive predictable delivery against hiring targets across high-volume, niche scientific/technical, and executive searches; personally lead select senior searches Build and continuously improve recruiting processes, interviewer training, and candidate experience from first touch to signed offer Define and report on TA metrics (time-to-fill, pipeline conversion, offer-accept rate, quality of hire, cost per hire, source effectiveness) and use data to drive decisions Own the regional TA tech stack (ATS, sourcing and scheduling tools, AI-enabled recruiting tools) and vendor/agency relationships and budgets Build talent pipelines for hard-to-fill scientific and engineering disciplines through university partnerships, early-career programs, industry associations, and scientific communities Qualifications What You'll Bring 10+ years of talent acquisition experience, including 4+ years leading and scaling recruiting teams, ideally across multiple countries in the Americas A track record of delivering both volume and senior-level hiring in the life sciences, diagnostics, biotech, MedTech, scientific instrumentation, or technology sectors Experience recruiting specialized STEM talent — scientists, engineers, and technical field/service roles — and understanding of what motivates these candidate populations Experience partnering directly with C-level and VP stakeholders on workforce planning and org design in a global, matrixed organization Strong analytical and business/candidate advisory fluency: you run TA as “business” and “product” with dashboards, forecasts, and capacity models — not just requisitions – optimizing for TA efficiency and thoughtful design Deep knowledge of sourcing strategies, employer branding, structured interviewing, and modern recruiting tools Working knowledge of US employment and hiring compliance, including experience in a regulated and/or federal contractor environment; familiarity with Canadian and Latin American hiring practices strongly preferred Exceptional communication and influencing skills; able to set direction, gain buy-in, and hold a high bar with senior leaders Nice to Have Experience supporting hiring for Tech + Product + AI talent pillars in addition to Manufacturing, R&D, Commercial, and G&A functions Experience scaling hiring in key Americas markets outside the US (e.g., Mexico, Brazil, Canada) Experience with TA Advisor models and behaviors Experience implementing or migrating an ATS and building TA analytics from the ground up Additional Details This job has a full time weekly schedule. It includes the option to work remotely. Applications for this job will be accepted until at least September 18, 2026 or until the job is no longer posted. The full-time equivalent pay range for this position is $181,200.00 - $339,750.00/yr plus eligibility for bonus, stock and benefits. Our pay ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. During the hiring process, a recruiter can share more about the specific pay range for a preferred location. Pay and benefit information by country are available at: https://careers.agilent.com/locations Agilent Technologies, Inc. is an Equal Employment Opportunity and merit-based employer that values individuals of all backgrounds at all levels. All individuals, regardless of personal characteristics, are encouraged to apply. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, pregnancy, race, religion or religious creed, color, gender, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, registered domestic partner status, age, sexual orientation, military or veteran status, protected veteran status, or any other basis protected by federal, state, local law, ordinance, or regulation and will not be discriminated against on these bases. The federal division of Chugach Alaska Corporation, CGS has been supporting critical missions as a government contractor for over 25 years. Our focus is to support facility maintenance, IT/technical services, construction and education. We are proud to have built, and continue to foster, an incredibly talented team spanning across the globe in hundreds of different fields – each team member proud to serve our country with first-class business services, while also making a difference for our Chugach shareholders. At CGS, empowering employees is a part of our core, and that focus is one of the ways we build and foster high-performing teams. We empower our employees through competitive compensation and benefits package, professional growth opportunities, truthful communication, and more! If you are looking for an opportunity to serve something bigger than yourself; if you want your day job to be one that creates meaningful value; if you are looking for an environment that highly values employees and respects individual differences – then Chugach Government Solutions may be the right fit for you! Position Location Position is located onsite in San Diego, Ca. Job Overview Responsible for supervising employees and performing day-to-day operations to accomplish contractual obligations for the NBPL Generators & HVAC Chiller Maintenance task order. Responsible for daily operation and oversight of all HVAC technicians, responsible asset management, and personnel administration. Duties also include maintenance of equipment in assistance to field technicians, administration of service call and preventative maintenance schedules and operations, response to service calls and quality control inspections of maintenance and repair activities. Also responsible for the generation of estimates for repairs discovered from preventative maintenance and service calls. Responsibilities Essential Job Duties: Act as official representative for CSE at NBPL Generators & HVAC Chiller Maintenance. Assist in generating schedules and proposals. Responsible for the timely completion and quality of all work and services performed by CSE and its subcontractors. Recommendations for all personnel actions and programs for CSE employees on the task order. Responsible for the health and welfare of CSE personnel on the job, as well as for compliance with all OSHA and EM385 requirements in the workplace. Responsible for compliance with all environmental laws, and directives as applicable to the environmental for work performed by DBSI and subcontractor personnel. Responsible for assistance in all documents and reports submitted to the government and CSE. Accountable for all activities involved in the performance of the NBPL Generators & HVAC Chiller Maintenance task order. Pay Range: $85K - 95K DOE Job Requirements Mandatory: High school diploma or equivalent. Current Secret Security Clearance. At least 8 years of progressively responsible experience in government contracting, with at least 5 years’ experience in Base Operating Services management (BOS). Strong proficiency in HVAC systems, Building Control systems, and energy management systems. Knowledge of generally accepted standards of workmanship in maintenance of facilities, including but not limited to electrical repairs. Knowledge of government contracting terminology and applications. Working knowledge of Microsoft Office, Excel, and PowerPoint software. Driver’s license with acceptable driving record. Preferred: Bachelor’s Degree or higher. Continuing education/ classes in engineering, general construction or business administration. Ten years’ experience at a supervisory level. Working Conditions: Work is performed mostly indoors. Outdoor work is subject to temperature extremes and inclement weather conditions. Work hours are subject to change, with weekend work or long hours as needed. Subject to hazards that may cause personal bodily harm; diseases, cuts, bruises, burns, common colds, influenza, dust, odors and elevated noise levels. Tasks may be performed on uneven, inclined, hard and soft-carpeted floors, cement structures and surfaces Must be able to work under, in or around buildings, structures, or fixtures, such as ducting systems, attics or crawl spaces. Physical Requirements: While performing duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to stand and/or walk for long periods at a time, sit, use of hands and fingers, handle, or feel objects, tools or controls, reach with hands and arms, climb stairs, climb ladders, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, talk or hear, or smell. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, pregnancy, disability, genetic factors, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law. Chugach will provide reasonable accommodations, according to applicable state and federal laws, to all qualified individuals with physical or mental disabilities. In compliance with the ADA Amendments Act (ADAAA), if you have a disability and would like to request an accommodation in order to apply for a position with Chugach Government Solutions or any of its subsidiaries, please email ada@chugachgov.com. This role involves exposure to international HR operations, including end-to-end HR processes, employee lifecycle management, and cross-border coordination to enhance employee experience. Job Snapshot Category Technology Company Folio3 Employment Type Full-time Work Mode Onsite Experience Level Up to 2 years Job Type Not specified Location N/A Open Date Not Specified Close Date Not Specified Salary N/A - N/A PKR / Monthly Eligibility & Requirements Skills HR Operations, Payroll Management, Recruitment, Employee Relations, Onboarding, Offboarding, HR Compliance, Communication Education Level Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field. Language Requirements English, Urdu Eligibility Bachelor’s degree with up to 2 years HR experience, strong English communication, and ability to work flexible CST overlapping hours. Requirements Up to 2 years of HR operations or generalist experience Strong English communication skills (verbal and written) Solid understanding of HR processes, payroll cycles, and employee engagement practices Ability to work flexible hours including overlap with US CST time zone Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or related field Responsibilities Manage end-to-end HR processes including onboarding, offboarding, and employee records Assist in payroll administration, contract management, and employee benefits across multiple regions Act as a point of contact for employee queries and engagement initiatives Support HR operations for international offices (US, UK, Canada, UAE, KSA) ensuring policy compliance Coordinate with recruitment agencies for offshore hiring and talent acquisition needs Benefits Health coverage, performance increments/bonuses, paid leave and employee engagement benefits — Reported Contact Information N/A Company Details Folio3 Why this matters This job page shows the public-facing details in a stable layout so visitors can review the role, then open the official application link when ready. More About This Job The HR Executive role at Folio3 can be a strong opportunity for an early-career HR professional who wants exposure beyond routine local HR work. Because the position supports teams across several countries, candidates need to show that they can communicate clearly, stay organized and handle employee matters carefully across different time zones and working environments. Looking for more verified career opportunities across Pakistan? Explore the latest private and public sector openings on Explore Latest Jobs on PehlePakistan What Does This Role Mean in Practice? Working with international teams means the HR Executive may deal with different employee expectations, payroll schedules, policies and communication styles. For a candidate, this means knowing HR basics is not enough. You should understand how onboarding, employee records, payroll coordination and employee queries connect with the overall employee experience. Strong attention to detail is especially important because small errors in records, contracts or payroll information can create bigger problems when teams are working across several countries. What Should You Prepare Before Applying? Before applying, review the practical side of HR operations. Useful Areas To Revise Include: Employee onboarding and offboarding Payroll cycles Employee documentation Contract administration Employee engagement Recruitment coordination Basic HR compliance Employee query handling Record management You should also understand why HR policies can differ between countries. You do not need to be an expert in every country's labor laws, but familiarity with international HR practices can make your profile stronger. How to Improve Your CV Keep your CV focused on actual HR work instead of filling it with general terms such as "good communication" or "team player." If you have previous HR experience, explain what you handled. For example, highlight experience with employee onboarding, payroll support, maintaining HR records, recruitment coordination, employee engagement activities or answering staff queries. If you have worked with overseas employees or international stakeholders, make that experience easy to find. Candidates with limited experience can also highlight internships, HR projects, university activities or administrative work that required communication, documentation and confidentiality. Working With Global Teams One important part of this position is coordination with teams in different regions. That can require flexibility in working hours, particularly when communication with the US team is needed. Before applying, make sure you are comfortable managing occasional schedule overlap and communicating professionally through email, calls and online meetings. International HR work also requires cultural awareness. A communication style that works well with one team may need adjustment when dealing with employees from another country. Interview Preparation The exact interview questions cannot be confirmed in advance. Candidates are more likely to be assessed on their understanding of HR operations, communication ability and how they respond to practical employee situations. Prepare Examples Involving: An employee joining or leaving the company A payroll discrepancy An employee asking about a policy Missing or incorrect HR documentation Coordinating with a recruitment agency Handling confidential employee information Communicating with an overseas team Managing several HR tasks with competing deadlines When answering, explain the situation, what action you would take and why. Avoid giving only textbook definitions. Practical answers usually make it easier to demonstrate that you understand how HR work happens in a real workplace. How to Apply Candidates should use the Folio3 job page or careers system rather than relying on the company's general information email. Before Submitting Your Application: Prepare an updated CV. Keep your personal and contact information accurate. Add your education details. Include relevant HR experience clearly. Add your LinkedIn profile if requested. Review your application before submission. Make sure your phone number and email remain active for recruitment communication. Common Mistakes to Avoid Avoid using the same generic CV for every HR role. Other Common Mistakes Include: Claiming payroll knowledge without understanding payroll cycles Ignoring the international nature of the position Weak written English in the application Not explaining practical HR experience Providing unclear employment dates Overstating knowledge of international labor laws Applying without considering CST working-hour overlap Career Growth International HR operations experience can help build a path toward roles such as HR Generalist, Senior HR Executive, HR Operations Specialist, People Operations Specialist or broader HR business-partner positions. Exposure to different countries can also help candidates understand how global companies manage policies, employees and workplace processes across multiple locations. FAQs Can someone with limited HR experience apply? The position is aimed at candidates with early-career HR experience. Relevant internships, HR operations exposure and practical understanding of employee processes can strengthen an application. Is international HR experience mandatory? Previous international exposure can be useful, but candidates can still strengthen their profile by understanding cross-border HR operations and showing that they can learn different policies and processes. Why is strong English important for this role? The position involves communication with employees and teams in several countries. Clear written and spoken English helps reduce misunderstandings and supports professional coordination. What should I know about payroll before the interview? Understand the basic payroll cycle, employee data accuracy, attendance or leave inputs, deductions and why payroll information needs careful review before processing. Do I need to know labor laws for every country mentioned? Deep expertise in every jurisdiction is unlikely to be realistic for an early-career candidate. Focus on understanding that HR practices differ between countries and that local requirements must be checked before making decisions. What can I highlight if I have mostly recruitment experience?
